Categories.value: Media from YouTube|Videos of 2011|Uploaded with video2commons|Videos of physics|License reviewed by YouTubeReviewBot|Videos of unsolved problems in physics

ImageDescription.value:
Table of content:

00:11 Stepper motor 01:27 Shortening the turn-on time 02:16 Enabling inductors simultaneously 03:19 Altering the direction of rotation 04:29 Software modes stepper motor 06:37 Rotation by repelling forces 09:04 Sensor disc 09:29 Electronic commutation 11:07 Brake pedal 11:31 Automatic speed control 12:33 Revolution counter 14:59 Electric input power 17:33 Losses at the power transistors (temperature) 18:28 Mechanical output power (efficiency) 19:28 Software modes commutated motor 22:48 Oscillograph turn-on times

The functionality of an electric motor is treated at this video. The motor is converted from a stepper motor into an electronically commutated motor in progress of the film. In addition, the efficiency of the motor is determined. To do so, the electric input power and the mechanical output power are measured. The used materials of the electric motor are as simple as possible to be able to do a reverse engeneering. The functionality is demonstrated by using a self-made revolution counter, digital multimeter, LEDs and an oscilloscope. An ATmega8A microcontroller is used to control the motor by software.

This little electric motor is a test model of an electric vehicle, which is built as an open source project by now.
